changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from CV Intoxicating Substances Reference: benzodiazepines (and the flumazenil caveat), barbiturates and Z-drugs, and GHB/GBL/1,4-butanediol including its distinct withdrawal emergency.

summary: A shared CNS-depressant toxidrome over agents with sharply different safety margins. Isolated benzodiazepine or Z-drug overdose is one of the safer ingestions in toxicology (a respiratory-depression ceiling); isolated barbiturate overdose is genuinely lethal (no ceiling). GHB is defined by its kinetics — abrupt coma, abrupt awakening — and its withdrawal is a separate, life-threatening emergency.
whyThisMatters: The mental model that "sedatives are basically safe" is true for benzodiazepines and Z-drugs alone and dangerously false for barbiturates and for any sedative co-ingested with alcohol or opioids — which is most real overdoses. Two specific traps: reaching for flumazenil in a mixed or chronic-use overdose (where the antidote causes more harm than the drug), and mistaking GHB withdrawal for a milder cousin of alcohol withdrawal when it is faster in onset and just as lethal.
clinicalTakeaway: Supportive care — airway positioning, monitoring, and intubation for genuine airway compromise — covers the large majority. Deep coma, hyperreflexia/clonus, or cardiovascular instability in a supposed isolated benzodiazepine overdose means look for a co-ingestant, not severe benzodiazepine toxicity. Reserve flumazenil for isolated, benzodiazepine-naive, iatrogenic reversal and call poison control first. Treat isolated barbiturate overdose as potentially lethal — ventilatory and vasopressor support, and for phenobarbital urinary alkalinization plus multi-dose activated charcoal (hemodialysis if refractory). Recognize the abrupt-coma / abrupt-awakening GHB pattern, and treat GHB withdrawal aggressively with high-dose benzodiazepines, escalating faster than an alcohol-withdrawal protocol.

rows: GABA-A positive allosteric modulator (increases channel opening frequency) — a respiratory-depression ceiling as monotherapy. Isolated overdose: sedation, ataxia, slurred speech, rarely more. Co-ingestion (alcohol, opioids) removes the safety margin and drives most fatal benzodiazepine-involved deaths

Supportive care suffices for most. GI decontamination not routine (aspiration risk). Flumazenil is RELATIVELY CONTRAINDICATED in unknown/mixed overdose, chronic use, seizure history, or QRS prolongation — precipitates seizures and life-threatening withdrawal; meta-analysis found more serious adverse events than placebo (NNH ~50). Reserve for isolated, benzo-naive, iatrogenic reversal; consult poison control. Intubate for true airway compromise (usually a co-ingestant)

Increase GABA-A channel-opening DURATION and directly activate the channel at high dose — NO ceiling effect, narrow therapeutic index. Dose-dependent progression: sedation → respiratory failure → hypotension → cardiogenic shock; potentially fatal in isolated ingestion

Airway/ventilatory support, vasopressors for cardiogenic shock. For phenobarbital specifically: urinary alkalinization + multi-dose activated charcoal (enterohepatic recirculation, pH-dependent renal clearance). Extracorporeal removal (hemodialysis/hemoperfusion) for massive refractory toxicity
Selective alpha-1 GABA-A subunit — behave like low-toxicity benzodiazepines as monotherapy; coma / respiratory depression / cardiovascular instability rare alone

Supportive care. Flumazenil may be cautiously considered for isolated Z-drug overdose (cross-reacts at the benzodiazepine site) with the same seizure/withdrawal caveats — no effect on barbiturates (separate receptor site)

GABA-B agonist at exogenous concentrations (GBL and 1,4-BD are prodrugs). Very short half-life (~27-30 min) → narrow, unpredictable dose-response. Signature: abrupt-onset coma with rapid spontaneous recovery — deeply unresponsive one hour, abruptly awake and trying to self-extubate the next. Not detected on routine screens

Supportive care, no antidote; airway support / ventilation for severe intoxication. Bradycardia → atropine; hypotension → IV fluids. Because of the abrupt-awakening pattern, sedation is often unnecessary during ventilation — plan for sudden extubation attempts

body.text: GHB withdrawal is a distinct, life-threatening emergency (unlike acute GHB intoxication). It can progress within hours of last use to severe agitation, autonomic instability, and delirium resembling severe alcohol withdrawal — but faster in onset and needing benzodiazepine dosing that goes higher and faster than alcohol-withdrawal protocols. Refractory cases have used barbiturates, baclofen, propofol, dexmedetomidine, or thiopental-induced burst-suppression coma.
Reach for flumazenil far less often than intuition suggests. In real-world mixed overdoses — which is most of them — the antidote causes more harm than the drug it is reversing.
